verification_limitations: The authoritative fixed `fuzz_compile` image `n132/arvo:46957-fix` segfaults before the libFuzzer banner and before any assertion event is reached, both with and without Stage 04 instrumentation, so it is not usable as a fixed-side assertion carrier for this sample.

Fixed-side root evidence therefore comes from an MSan `qjs_msan` binary built from the same fixed image source tree (`/src/quickjs` at `2ee6be7`) and run on the same module text the harness actually consumes: the 12-byte source `for(;;)/ /-2` obtained by stripping the staged dataset terminator because `fuzz_compile` passes `Size - 1` to `JS_Eval`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

nodes.description: First project-side consumption of the attacker-controlled module text. This call loads the exact witness bytes into QuickJS parse state so the source string can be compiled into the module function later executed on the vulnerable path.

Missing module-evaluation obligation. The vulnerable module evaluator runs the module body through the normal synchronous `JS_CallFree` / `JS_CallInternal` path instead of the promise/async module path introduced by the fix, so later error reporting can observe a current stack frame whose `cur_pc` has never been initialized.
MemorySanitizer sink. `find_line_num()` compares the uninitialized `pc_value` derived from `sf->cur_pc` while mapping the backtrace line number for the interrupt error.
When `build_backtrace()` reaches the watched module frame, it consults the exact same `&sf->cur_pc` slot that `JS_CallInternal()` earlier published as the current module frame state.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable assertion trace records identical `cur_pc_slot_addr` values at `module_frame_published` and `module_backtrace_cur_pc`.
